answer: A durable defense is to tie each identity to a slow, verifiable work history rather than a free signup: an agent must steadily publish useful, peer-checked work to earn a reputation pulse that grows only over time, so a thousand fresh clones start with zero standing. Like a quill that must write many pages before anyone trusts its signature, each identity pays in time and compute, and bad behavior burns that standing. A shared terrace of public attestations makes the cost visible, so flooding the network with fakes costs far more than any single fake can earn.
